# Strategic Research Framework

### 1. Core Objective & Business Context

- **Business problem:** Track the strength of Epic Games and Fortnite among Indian mobile gamers within the wider battle royale market, while understanding how usage, social play, live-service updates, collaborations, and in-game spending influence brand loyalty.
- **Why this matters now:** Fortnite competes in a fast-moving category where player attention can shift between titles such as Fortnite, BGMI/PUBG, Free Fire, and Apex Legends. A recurring tracker is needed to distinguish short-term campaign or season effects from durable changes in awareness, consideration, usage, loyalty, and competitive position.
- **Decision enabled:** The research will guide marketing, partnership, collaboration, campaign, community, and retention strategy by showing which audiences are most valuable, what keeps them engaged, and where Fortnite is gaining or losing relevance.
- **Tracking principle:** Maintain an identical core brand-health module across waves, while allowing a small rotating module for current campaigns, collaborations, seasonal updates, monetisation initiatives, or emerging competitors.

### 2. Secondary Research Snapshot

- **Mobile remains a major growth and monetisation engine:** Newzoo forecasts mobile games revenue to reach $121.1 billion in 2026, indicating that mobile engagement and monetisation should remain central measures in this tracker. — Newzoo. ([newzoo.com](https://newzoo.com/articles/global-games-market-2025))
- **The global games market continues to expand:** Newzoo estimates the global games market at $188.8 billion in 2025, with growth shaped by changing platform dynamics and continued mobile monetisation. This supports tracking platform choice and movement between mobile, PC, and console rather than treating mobile behavior in isolation. — Newzoo. ([newzoo.com](https://newzoo.com/articles/global-games-market-189-billion-2025/))
- **Battle royale is a multi-title competitive ecosystem:** Newzoo’s battle royale analysis specifically compares leading PC and mobile titles and identifies regional differences in Fortnite and PUBG performance. The study should therefore measure unaided awareness, aided awareness, usage, consideration, and perceived differentiation across the competitive set. — Newzoo. ([resources.newzoo.com](https://resources.newzoo.com/the-rise-of-battle-royale))
- **India is a high-reach but relatively low-monetisation gaming market:** Available market reporting describes India as a very large mobile-download market, while revenue per player remains comparatively low. This makes payment behavior, purchase conversion, spend occasions, and barriers to spending important tracking variables rather than relying only on stated loyalty. — Sensor Tower reporting summarized by Game Developer Reports. ([gamedevreports.substack.com](https://gamedevreports.substack.com/i/167151250/market-overview))
- **In-game monetisation and brand integrations are becoming more important in India:** Recent Indian gaming coverage reports rising average revenue among paying users and a projected shift toward greater in-app-purchase contribution. The tracker should connect spending with perceived value, cosmetics, events, collaborations, and engagement rather than measuring spend as a standalone behavior. — The Economic Times, citing the Bitkraft–Redseer report. ([economictimes.indiatimes.com](http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/online-gaming-india-krafton-bgmi-rooter-bitkraft-redseer-nazara-in-app-purchases-driving-growth/articleshow/126368318.cms))
- **Fortnite’s ecosystem extends beyond the core battle royale mode:** Epic’s creator-economy model distributes engagement-based revenue to eligible island creators, making creator-made experiences and social participation relevant parts of Fortnite’s brand proposition. — Epic Games. ([fortnite.com](https://www.fortnite.com/news/introducing-the-creator-economy-2-0), [fortnite.com](https://www.fortnite.com/news/fortnite-engagement-payout-update?lang=en-US))

### 3. Research Type & Methodology

- **Study type:** Brand Health / Tracking combined with Usage & Attitude, Competitive Landscape, and selected Customer Experience-style engagement measures.
- **Discrete stimuli counted:** Zero. The study is tracking existing brands, behaviors, perceptions, and market participation; it does not require respondents to evaluate specific advertisements, packs, concepts, or other discrete stimuli.
- **Research design:** A linear, modular tracking questionnaire with a consistent core across waves. Cell-based designs such as monadic, sequential monadic, A/B, paired comparison, and split-cell testing do not apply because there are no discrete stimuli to show.
- **Why this approach:** The central decision is to monitor movement in brand health and explain why that movement occurs. A modular tracking design will provide clean wave-to-wave comparison while linking awareness and consideration to actual play frequency, recent usage, switching, social behavior, live-service engagement, and spending.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Single-wave U&A study:** Useful for a broad behavioral snapshot, but weaker for identifying whether Fortnite’s position is improving or declining over time.
  - **Concept or campaign testing:** Appropriate when specific creative or partnership assets must be evaluated, but not suitable for the current always-on brand-health objective.
  - **Segmentation-first study:** Could identify player personas in depth, but should follow the tracker or use a limited attitudinal battery because the immediate priority is monitoring brand and competitive movement.
- **User control:** If you prefer a different methodology, such as a standalone campaign test or a deeper player segmentation study, it can be switched before the research brief is generated.
- **Survey design logic:** Use a modular funnel: category behavior before brand measures; unaided awareness before aided awareness; usage before attitudes; attitudes before loyalty and advocacy; and behavioral spend questions before asking for explanations. Keep the core battery stable across waves and rotate only timely modules such as seasonal updates, major collaborations, creator experiences, or campaign exposure.
- **Wave design:** Establish a baseline wave, then repeat the core instrument in subsequent waves. Use identical wording and scales for trend KPIs. Add wave identifiers and field-period markers so changes can be interpreted alongside season launches, partnerships, esports moments, and major product updates.
- **Indian panel and device context:** Surveys will be deployed to verified Indian respondents through the SuperJ mobile application and web. Age, gender, city, and NCCS targeting will be enforced by the audience system before the survey begins, so these should not be re-collected in the questionnaire.
- **Quality controls:** Include platform-compliant attention checks, speeder detection, straight-line detection, open-end gibberish screening, and checks for implausible gaming behavior. Use short screens, minimal grids, fully labeled five-point scales, behavioral validation, and tap-friendly response formats for smartphone completion.

### 4. Target Audience Profile

- **Who we are asking:** Indian mobile gamers spanning frequent, occasional, and lapsed players; current Fortnite players; players of competing battle royale titles; and relevant parents or household decision-makers for younger players where permission and platform policy allow.
- **Behavioral coverage:** Include players across different session frequencies, play durations, multiplayer patterns, game genres, platform mixes, recent game switching, uninstalling and returning, and in-app-purchase behavior.
- **Competitive relevance:** Ensure the audience includes people with direct experience of Fortnite and competing games such as BGMI/PUBG, Free Fire, and Apex Legends, rather than relying only on general gaming awareness.
- **Why these people hold the answers:** Current players can assess Fortnite’s live experience and loyalty drivers; lapsed players can explain churn and re-entry barriers; competitor players reveal conquest opportunities; and household decision-makers can illuminate spending permissions and perceptions around younger players.
- **Must-have screening criteria:** Recent mobile gaming activity; sufficient familiarity with at least one tracked game or gaming brand; ability to identify the games they currently or recently play; and, for player-level modules, a minimum recent usage threshold that is consistent across waves.
- **Indian segmentation lens:** Analyze results by metro and tier-1/2/3 location, region, NCCS, age band, gaming frequency, current Fortnite usage, competing-game usage, and payer versus non-payer status. These are audience cuts supplied or enforced through the platform’s targeting system where applicable.

### 5. Key Information Areas & Data Architecture

- **Category and platform behavior:** Capture mobile gaming frequency, session length, time of day, genres, titles, and platform use → reveals the size and habits of the addressable gaming audience → informs channel planning and audience prioritization.
- **Unaided and aided brand funnel:** Measure spontaneous awareness first, followed by aided awareness, familiarity, consideration, current usage, recent usage, and likelihood to continue → shows where Fortnite and Epic Games win or lose in the funnel → guides brand-building and acquisition strategy.
- **Competitive repertoire and switching:** Record games played alongside Fortnite, recent switching, uninstalling, returning, and reasons for movement → identifies competitive displacement and retention risks → supports conquest, win-back, and product communication decisions.
- **Brand associations and differentiation:** Measure perceptions such as fun, social connection, creativity, variety, competitiveness, cultural relevance, trust, value, and distinctiveness → explains what Fortnite owns versus what competitors own → guides positioning, partnerships, and campaign messaging.
- **Live-service engagement:** Track awareness and participation in seasonal updates, limited-time events, collaborations, creator-made experiences, esports, and community activities → identifies which ecosystem elements strengthen engagement → informs partnership and content investment.
- **Social and community behavior:** Measure squad play, friend invitations, voice or text interaction, creator influence, sharing, streaming, and community participation → reveals the social mechanisms behind retention and advocacy → supports community and creator strategy.
- **In-app purchase behavior:** Measure payer status, purchase frequency, recent purchase occasion, broad INR spend bands, purchase categories, perceived value, and barriers → links monetisation to engagement and brand perceptions → informs cosmetic, collaboration, offer, and value communication strategy.
- **Loyalty and advocacy:** Track likelihood to continue, recommend, invite friends, return after a break, and choose Fortnite over alternatives → provides leading indicators of retention and organic growth → supports investment decisions and wave-to-wave performance evaluation.

### 6. Survey Flow & Question Design Approach

- **Phase 1 — Warm-up and Screening:** Establish recent mobile gaming behavior, frequency, platforms, and relevant game usage. Use behavior-based qualification before asking brand opinions.
- **Phase 2 — Category Context:** Measure genres played, battle royale participation, session patterns, social play, and game repertoire. This creates the competitive context before Fortnite or Epic Games are named in detail.
- **Phase 3 — Unaided Brand Health:** Capture unaided awareness of gaming companies, games, and battle royale titles, followed by spontaneous associations and top-of-mind consideration.
- **Phase 4 — Aided Funnel and Competitive Benchmarking:** Measure aided awareness, familiarity, consideration, current usage, recent usage, preference, perceived differentiation, and brand associations for Epic Games, Fortnite, and selected competitors.
- **Phase 5 — Fortnite Engagement Deep Dive:** Among relevant respondents, assess play frequency, session behavior, multiplayer participation, seasonal content, collaborations, creator experiences, community behavior, switching, uninstalling, and returning.
- **Phase 6 — Monetisation and Value:** Measure whether respondents make in-app purchases, recent purchase behavior, broad INR spend bands, purchase motivations, value perceptions, and barriers. Use optional-feeling wording for spend questions and avoid making payment behavior feel judgmental.
- **Phase 7 — Loyalty, Advocacy, and Open Ends:** Measure likelihood to continue, recommend, invite friends, return, and choose Fortnite over alternatives. End with short open-ended probes on the strongest reason to play, the biggest frustration, and one change that would increase engagement.
- **Phase 8 — Rotating Wave Module:** Add a small wave-specific module for a campaign, collaboration, seasonal event, creator initiative, or competitive development. Keep this separate from the stable tracking core so trend KPIs remain comparable.
- **Estimated structure:** A smartphone-friendly instrument of approximately 15–25 questions, designed for an 8–12 minute completion window. The final question count will depend on routing between current players, lapsed players, competitor players, non-payers, payers, and parents or household decision-makers.
- **Scale design:** Prefer fully labeled five-point unipolar scales, behavioral frequency questions, forced trade-offs where useful, and short open-ended probes. Avoid long agree/disagree grids because positive-end responding and acquiescence can inflate apparent brand strength.

### 7. Expected Insights & Business Decisions Enabled

- **You will be able to:** Track unaided and aided awareness, familiarity, consideration, usage, loyalty, advocacy, and perceived differentiation for Epic Games and Fortnite across waves.
- **You will be able to:** Identify which Indian gamer segments are most engaged with Fortnite, which are drifting toward competitors, and which are high-potential non-users.
- **You will be able to:** Diagnose whether changes in loyalty are linked to play frequency, social participation, seasonal content, collaborations, creator experiences, value perceptions, or competitive activity.
- **You will be able to:** Quantify the role of in-app purchases, broad INR spending behavior, cosmetic value, and collaboration-driven excitement in engagement and retention.
- **You will be able to decide:** Which audiences should receive priority in marketing and campaign planning.
- **You will be able to decide:** Which partnerships, collaborations, creator programs, and community initiatives are most aligned with the strongest engagement drivers.
- **You will be able to decide:** Whether Fortnite’s positioning should emphasize social play, creativity, competition, cultural relevance, live events, variety, or another differentiated strength.
- **You will be able to decide:** Where retention, win-back, and competitive-conquest activity should be focused.
- **Key hypotheses being tested:**
  - Fortnite has stronger spontaneous awareness than most competing battle royale titles among active Indian mobile gamers.
  - Fortnite’s differentiation is driven more by its ecosystem, collaborations, creativity, and social experience than by battle royale gameplay alone.
  - Frequent multiplayer and community participation are associated with stronger loyalty and advocacy.
  - Seasonal updates and collaborations increase engagement, but their effect may be stronger among existing players than among lapsed or competitor-only players.
  - Spending is influenced by perceived cosmetic and event value, not only by play frequency.
  - Lapsed players are more likely to return when the trigger is a major update, collaboration, friend invitation, or new content experience.
- **KPIs to report:** Unaided awareness; aided awareness; familiarity; consideration; current usage; recent usage; usage frequency; competitive repertoire; Fortnite share of recent play; switch-in and switch-out rates; key association scores; differentiation index; likelihood to continue; recommendation and advocacy indicators; multiplayer participation; seasonal or collaboration engagement; payer incidence; recent purchase incidence; broad spend bands; value perception; and top reasons for switching, returning, or purchasing.
- **Tracking outputs:** Report absolute wave scores, wave-over-wave movement, competitor gaps, segment differences, and driver relationships. Interpret changes against field timing and major gaming-market events rather than treating every movement as a permanent brand shift.

turns.research_brief:
# Research Brief: Fortnite & Epic Games Brand Health Among Indian Mobile Gamers

### **Background & Context**

Epic Games and Fortnite operate in a fast-moving mobile gaming environment where player attention can move between Fortnite, BGMI/PUBG, Free Fire, Apex Legends, and other live-service titles. The business trigger is the need to distinguish short-term effects from durable changes in awareness, consideration, usage, loyalty, advocacy, and competitive position across repeated waves.

The wider games market continues to expand. Newzoo estimates the global games market at $188.8 billion in 2025 and forecasts growth to $206.5 billion by 2028, with 3.6 billion players in 2025. Mobile engagement and monetisation remain strategically important, making platform behavior, session frequency, and mobile spending essential tracker measures. According to Newzoo, mobile games revenue is forecast to reach $121.1 billion in 2026. ([newzoo.com](https://newzoo.com/reports/global-games-market-report), [newzoo.com](https://newzoo.com/articles/global-games-market-2025))

India is a high-reach gaming market with substantial growth potential. BITKRAFT and Redseer project India’s digital gaming market to double by FY2030, with battle royale and hybrid-casual titles among the growth areas. Sensor Tower also identifies India as a global leader in mobile-game downloads while highlighting continuing opportunities to improve monetisation. ([bitkraft.vc](https://bitkraft.vc/insights/bitkraft-india-report), [sensortower.com](https://sensortower.com/ja/state-of-mobile-games-in-india-2025-report))

India’s monetisation environment makes payer behavior especially important to track. The Economic Times, citing BITKRAFT–Redseer, reports that average revenue per paying user has increased materially and that in-app purchases are expected to become a larger contributor to Indian gaming revenue. Fortnite’s mobile ecosystem also includes Battle Royale, creative experiences, social play, live events, and optional in-app purchases, making loyalty broader than gameplay frequency alone. ([economictimes.indiatimes.com](http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/online-gaming-india-krafton-bgmi-rooter-bitkraft-redseer-nazara-in-app-purchases-driving-growth/articleshow/126368318.cms), [play.google.com](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en-IN&id=com.epicgames.fortnite))

---

### **Research Objectives**

Based on the approved strategic framework, this study will address the following business objectives.

#### **Strategic Objectives**

1. **Measure** the strength of Epic Games and Fortnite’s brand-health funnel among Indian mobile gamers in order to guide brand, acquisition, retention, and competitive strategy.
2. **Quantify** Fortnite’s position within the Indian battle royale ecosystem in order to identify opportunities for growth, conquest, and win-back.
3. **Determine** which gameplay, social, creator, collaboration, seasonal, and monetisation experiences strengthen loyalty in order to prioritise marketing and product investment.
4. **Identify** the behavioral and perceptual drivers of continued usage, advocacy, switching, and return in order to improve retention and reactivation.
5. **Assess** how in-app purchasing and perceived value contribute to engagement and loyalty in order to inform cosmetic, collaboration, event, and offer strategy.

#### **Tactical Objectives**

1. **Measure** unaided awareness, aided awareness, familiarity, consideration, current usage, recent usage, and preference for Epic Games, Fortnite, and tracked competitors.
2. **Map** the competitive repertoire of Indian mobile gamers, including concurrent usage of Fortnite, BGMI/PUBG, Free Fire, Apex Legends, and other relevant games.
3. **Quantify** Fortnite’s share of recent play, frequency of play, session duration, multiplayer participation, and platform mix.
4. **Identify** the strongest associations linked to Fortnite, including fun, creativity, social connection, variety, competition, cultural relevance, trust, value, and distinctiveness.
5. **Measure** awareness and participation in seasonal updates, limited-time events, collaborations, creator-made experiences, esports, streaming, and community activity.
6. **Determine** the triggers and barriers associated with switching, uninstalling, lapsed usage, and returning to Fortnite.
7. **Assess** the relationship between squad play, friend invitations, creator influence, sharing, streaming, and community participation and stronger loyalty or advocacy.
8. **Quantify** payer incidence, purchase frequency, recent purchase occasions, broad INR spending bands, purchase categories, and perceived value.
9. **Identify** barriers to in-app spending, including price, payment friction, low perceived value, lack of interest, parental or household restrictions, and preference for free content.
10. **Measure** likelihood to continue, recommend, invite friends, return after a break, and choose Fortnite over alternatives using loyalty and advocacy indicators.
11. **Validate** whether Fortnite’s differentiation is driven more by its wider ecosystem, collaborations, creativity, and social experience than by battle royale gameplay alone.
12. **Compare** current Fortnite players, lapsed players, competitor-only players, frequent gamers, occasional gamers, payers, and non-payers to identify high-value growth segments.

---

### **Type of Study**

We will conduct a **Brand Health / Tracking study combined with Usage & Attitude, Competitive Landscape, and selected loyalty and engagement measures**. This is the right study type because the business needs a stable wave-to-wave view of brand salience, awareness, consideration, usage, perception, loyalty, advocacy, competitive movement, and monetisation behavior.

The study contains **zero discrete stimuli**. Respondents will not evaluate advertisements, concepts, packs, price cells, or campaign assets. The emphasis is on existing brands, real-world gaming behavior, perceptions, experiences, and movement between titles.

---

### **Survey Design Approach** (Marketing Research Methodology)

The selected approach is a **linear structured questionnaire using a modular funnel and tracking-wave design**. It fits this objective because the study must measure natural behavior before brand evaluation, establish a consistent core across waves, and explain why Fortnite’s brand-health scores change over time. The sequence will follow category behavior, unaided awareness, aided awareness, usage, perceptions, engagement, monetisation, loyalty, and advocacy.

The stable core will use identical wording and scales across waves for trend KPIs. A small rotating module may be added for current campaigns, collaborations, seasonal updates, creator initiatives, esports moments, monetisation programs, or emerging competitors. Platform targeting will enforce age, gender, city, and NCCS quotas before the survey begins; these variables will not be re-collected in the questionnaire.

**Design Selection:** The selected design is a **zero-stimulus modular tracking design**. Since there are no discrete stimuli to compare, monadic, sequential monadic, paired comparison, A/B, and split-cell designs are not appropriate.

**Alternatives considered:**
- **Standalone U&A study:** Not chosen because it would provide a behavioral snapshot but would not support reliable wave-over-wave brand-health tracking.
- **Concept or campaign test:** Not chosen because no specific creative, collaboration asset, product concept, or advertisement is being evaluated.
- **Segmentation-first study:** Not chosen as the primary design because the immediate business need is tracking; a later segmentation analysis can use the behavioral and attitudinal battery collected here.

**Routing and controls:** Current Fortnite players, lapsed Fortnite players, competitor players, payers, non-payers, and respondents with creator or community engagement will receive relevant follow-up modules. The survey will use skip logic, branching, display logic, termination logic, filter logic, and completion logic. Attention checks will be embedded at approximately a 1:9 ratio. Speeder detection, straight-line detection, open-end gibberish screening, and implausible-behavior checks will be applied.

You can request a different methodology before generating the survey.

---

### **Question Flow & Survey Phases**

*   **Phase 1 — Warm-Up & Screening:** Confirm recent mobile gaming activity, gaming frequency, platform use, and familiarity with at least one tracked title. This establishes eligibility without beginning with brand judgments.
*   **Phase 2 — Category Usage & Competitive Context:** Measure genres played, session patterns, multiplayer behavior, game repertoire, time of day, recent switching, uninstalling, and returning. This provides the behavioral context for brand analysis.
*   **Phase 3 — Unaided Brand Health:** Capture spontaneous awareness of gaming companies, games, battle royale titles, and associations before showing or naming detailed brand lists.
*   **Phase 4 — Aided Funnel & Competitive Benchmarking:** Measure aided awareness, familiarity, consideration, current usage, recent usage, preference, perceived differentiation, and imagery for Epic Games, Fortnite, and relevant competitors.
*   **Phase 5 — Fortnite Engagement Deep Dive:** Among relevant respondents, assess play frequency, session duration, squad behavior, social interaction, seasonal updates, collaborations, creator experiences, community activity, esports, streaming, and sharing.
*   **Phase 6 — Switching, Churn & Return:** Identify reasons for switching, stopping, uninstalling, reducing usage, returning, or choosing a competitor. This phase will support retention, win-back, and conquest decisions.
*   **Phase 7 — Monetisation & Value:** Measure payer status, purchase frequency, broad INR spend bands, purchase occasions, purchase categories, perceived value, and barriers to in-app spending.
*   **Phase 8 — Loyalty, Advocacy & Open Ends:** Measure likelihood to continue, recommend, invite friends, return after a break, and choose Fortnite over alternatives. Short open-ended probes will capture the strongest reason to play, the biggest frustration, and the change most likely to increase engagement.
*   **Phase 9 — Rotating Wave Module:** Add a limited wave-specific module for a current collaboration, seasonal update, creator initiative, campaign, esports moment, or competitive development while keeping the tracking core unchanged.

The expected instrument is approximately **18–25 questions** and **8–12 minutes**, depending on routing. Break screens may be used between major modules if field testing indicates elevated fatigue.

---

### **Key Data Points to Measure**

#### **Primary Metrics (The KPIs)**

- **Unaided awareness** - enables top-of-mind salience benchmarking for Epic Games, Fortnite, and battle royale competitors.
- **Aided awareness** - measures total brand reach after prompted recognition.
- **Familiarity** - distinguishes superficial awareness from meaningful brand knowledge.
- **Consideration** - identifies brands entering the active choice set.
- **Current and recent usage** - measures present and recent competitive participation.
- **Fortnite share of recent play** - estimates Fortnite’s relative role within each respondent’s gaming repertoire.
- **Usage frequency and session duration** - identifies heavy, moderate, occasional, and lapsed player segments.
- **Competitive repertoire** - shows which titles are used alongside Fortnite and which competitors represent the greatest substitution risk.
- **Switch-in and switch-out rates** - identifies conquest and churn movement across waves.
- **Brand association scores** - measures perceptions of fun, creativity, social connection, variety, competition, cultural relevance, trust, value, and distinctiveness.
- **Differentiation index** - quantifies the attributes Fortnite owns more strongly than competitors.
- **Likelihood to continue** - provides a forward-looking retention indicator.
- **Recommendation likelihood and NPS** - measures advocacy potential using the standard 0–10 likelihood-to-recommend framework with reason probing.
- **Likelihood to invite friends** - measures social acquisition potential.
- **Likelihood to return after a break** - identifies reactivation potential among lapsed players.
- **Likelihood to choose Fortnite over alternatives** - measures competitive preference and choice strength.
- **Payer incidence** - quantifies the percentage of respondents making in-app purchases.
- **Recent purchase incidence and purchase frequency** - tracks monetisation participation over a defined recent period.
- **Broad INR spend bands** - supports payer segmentation without requiring sensitive exact-spend reporting.
- **Perceived value of cosmetics, events, collaborations, and other content** - connects spending to value perception.

#### **Supporting Metrics (Contextual Data)**

- Mobile gaming frequency and recency - provides a basis for qualifying active, occasional, and lapsed gamers.
- Platform mix across mobile, PC, and console - shows cross-platform behavior and the role of mobile within the wider gaming journey.
- Game genres played - identifies adjacent category interests and addressable audiences.
- Multiplayer and squad participation - explains the social foundation of retention.
- Voice, text, friend-invite, sharing, and streaming behavior - measures community and advocacy mechanisms.
- Seasonal-update awareness and participation - evaluates the role of live-service content.
- Collaboration awareness and participation - identifies partnership-driven engagement.
- Creator-made experience usage - measures the contribution of user-generated and creator-led content.
- Esports and competitive-content engagement - identifies the role of competitive culture in brand strength.
- Reasons for stopping, switching, uninstalling, and returning - diagnoses churn and win-back triggers.
- Reasons for not paying - identifies price, value, trust, payment, and permission barriers.
- Segment status - supports comparison of current players, lapsed players, competitor-only players, payers, non-payers, and high-frequency gamers.
- Field period and wave identifier - enables interpretation of changes alongside major seasons, launches, partnerships, and market events.

#### **Advanced Analytics We'll Apply**

- **Cross-tabulation and significance testing** to compare waves, cities, age brackets, gender, NCCS classes, usage frequency, payer status, and competitive segments.
- **Brand-funnel conversion analysis** to identify where Fortnite gains or loses respondents from awareness through loyalty.
- **Competitive gap analysis** to compare Fortnite with BGMI/PUBG, Free Fire, Apex Legends, and other tracked titles.
- **Driver analysis** to estimate which perceptions and behaviors are most strongly associated with loyalty, advocacy, and continued usage.
- **Switching-flow analysis** to map movement into and out of Fortnite across waves.
- **Segment profiling** to identify high-value players, growth prospects, lapsed users, competitor-only users, payers, and non-payers.
- **Semantic-differential and association analysis** to evaluate Fortnite’s perceptual territory relative to competitors.
- **Trend decomposition** to distinguish durable movement from effects associated with season launches, collaborations, campaigns, or major gaming events.
- **Open-end thematic and sentiment analysis** to identify recurring frustrations, motivations, return triggers, and unmet needs.

---

### **Expected Insights & Outcomes**

By the end of this study, you will possess the data to:

- **Validate:** Whether Fortnite has stronger spontaneous awareness than most competing battle royale titles among active Indian mobile gamers.
- **Validate:** Whether Fortnite’s differentiation is driven more by its ecosystem, collaborations, creativity, and social experience than by battle royale gameplay alone.
- **Validate:** Whether frequent multiplayer and community participation are associated with stronger loyalty and advocacy.
- **Validate:** Whether seasonal updates and collaborations increase engagement, and whether their effect is stronger among existing players than among lapsed or competitor-only players.
- **Validate:** Whether spending is influenced by perceived cosmetic and event value rather than by play frequency alone.
- **Validate:** Whether lapsed players are more likely to return after a major update, collaboration, friend invitation, or new content experience.

- **Decide:** Which Indian gamer segments should receive priority in marketing and campaign planning.
- **Decide:** Which partnerships, collaborations, creator programs, and community initiatives are most aligned with the strongest engagement drivers.
- **Decide:** Whether Fortnite’s positioning should emphasise social play, creativity, competition, cultural relevance, live events, variety, or another differentiated strength.
- **Decide:** Where retention, win-back, and competitive-conquest activity should be focused.
- **Decide:** How payer and non-payer strategies should differ based on perceived value, purchase behavior, and spending barriers.
- **Decide:** Which engagement and monetisation signals should be used as leading indicators in future tracking waves.

- **Strategize:** Brand communication, partnership, collaboration, creator, community, retention, win-back, monetisation, and competitive-conquest priorities using evidence from behavioral and perceptual movement.

**Key hypotheses being tested:**

1. Fortnite has stronger spontaneous awareness than most competing battle royale titles among active Indian mobile gamers.
2. Fortnite’s differentiation is driven more by its ecosystem, collaborations, creativity, and social experience than by battle royale gameplay alone.
3. Frequent multiplayer and community participation are associated with stronger loyalty and advocacy.
4. Seasonal updates and collaborations increase engagement, with stronger effects among existing players than among lapsed or competitor-only players.
5. Spending is influenced by perceived cosmetic and event value, not only by play frequency.
6. Lapsed players are more likely to return after a major update, collaboration, friend invitation, or new content experience.

**KPIs to report:** Unaided awareness; aided awareness; familiarity; consideration; current usage; recent usage; usage frequency; session duration; competitive repertoire; Fortnite share of recent play; switch-in and switch-out rates; key association scores; differentiation index; likelihood to continue; NPS and recommendation likelihood; likelihood to invite friends; likelihood to return; likelihood to choose Fortnite over alternatives; multiplayer participation; seasonal-update engagement; collaboration engagement; creator-experience engagement; community participation; payer incidence; recent purchase incidence; purchase frequency; broad INR spend bands; value perception; barriers to spending; and top reasons for switching, returning, stopping, or purchasing.

---

### **Methodology** [See why](hercules://explain?topic=Methodology)

We will deploy an **approximately 22-question, 8–12-minute** tracking survey on the **SuperJ mobile application and the web** to **450** verified Indian respondents for the baseline wave.

The questionnaire will use a zero-stimulus modular tracking design. The core order will be category behavior, unaided awareness, aided awareness, brand funnel, competitive benchmarking, Fortnite engagement, switching and churn, monetisation, loyalty, advocacy, and open-ended feedback. A rotating wave module may be added without changing the core KPI wording.

A total sample of 450 provides a practical directional baseline for overall tracking and enables comparison across major behavioral segments. Results will be interpreted using confidence intervals, significance testing, and segment base sizes rather than treating small subgroup differences as definitive. Future waves should preserve the core sample structure and field timing wherever possible.

The question mix will use behavioral frequency measures, fully labeled five-point scales, semantic-differential brand imagery measures, NPS, forced-choice comparisons where useful, and short open-ended probes at high-value diagnostic points. Long agree/disagree grids will be avoided to reduce acquiescence and positive-end response bias.

**Data Collection Approach:** SuperJ mobile application and web panel, with audience targeting enforced before survey start.

**Quality Controls:** Attention checks, speedster removal, straight-liner checks, open-end gibberish filtering, implausible gaming-behavior checks, duplicate screening, and routing validation.

---

### **Target Audience** [See why](hercules://explain?topic=Target+Audience)

The study will survey **Indian mobile gamers spanning frequent, occasional, and lapsed players; current Fortnite players; players of competing battle royale titles; and relevant household decision-makers for younger players where platform policy permits**. Because the platform serves respondents aged 18 and above, the sample will include adults who can report their own gaming behavior and spending decisions.

**Total Sample Size:** 450 respondents

**Geographic Focus:** Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Pune. These cities provide a focused metro sample for the baseline wave while avoiding an overly dispersed city design. The five city quotas sum to the full sample.

**Demographics:**

- **Gender:** 50% male and 50% female, represented as 225 male and 225 female respondents.
- **Age Range:** 18-24, 24-35, and 35-45. Quotas will be 180 respondents aged 18-24, 170 aged 24-35, and 100 aged 35-45.
- **Socioeconomic Class:** NCCS A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, and C1. Analysis will compare higher purchasing-power and broader mass-market segments without using Western income bands.

**Behavioral/Psychographic Filters:**

- Recent mobile gaming activity within the defined qualification period.
- Current, recent, or lapsed experience with Fortnite or at least one tracked competitor.
- Coverage of frequent, occasional, and lapsed mobile gamers.
- Coverage of current Fortnite players, competitor-only players, and former Fortnite players.
- Analysis by payer versus non-payer status.
- Analysis by multiplayer participation, creator influence, community participation, seasonal engagement, and collaboration awareness.

**Screening Criteria:**

- Must be an Indian resident aged 18 or above.
- Must have played mobile games recently or have qualifying recent gaming experience for the lapsed-player route.
- Must be able to identify at least one tracked gaming title or brand.
- Must meet the relevant current, recent, or lapsed usage threshold for the route they enter.
- Must pass platform attention, speed, consistency, and open-end quality checks.

**Statistical justification:** The audience payload mirrors the research brief exactly. Gender, age, and city are independent quota dimensions, and each dimension sums to the total sample of 450 respondents.

question_generation_instructions: METHODOLOGY: Brand Tracking — Brand Equity Funnel. Use the mandated order: unaided recall, aided awareness with non-aware termination, familiarity and usage, perception and equity, emotional connection, then loyalty and advocacy.
Generate exactly 22 respondent-facing questions using only the declared flow_keys. Do not add demographic, quota, or database-known targeting questions.
Keep core wording, response scales, brand lists, and KPI definitions stable across waves. Use compact bundled questions where a flow_key explicitly covers multiple related metrics.
BRAND_RECALL_UNAIDED must be open text and must precede BRAND_AWARENESS_AIDED. BRAND_AWARENESS_AIDED must be multi-select with an exclusive None of these option.
Use BRAND_TRIAL as a multi-select source and carry its selected options, in identical labels and order, into the vertical-ranking COMPETITOR_RATING_GRID.
Use recency anchoring for usage, recent play, stopping, switching, return, and purchase measures. Preserve the same time windows across waves.
Use BRAND_ATTRIBUTES as a concise multi-select association measure covering fun, creativity, social connection, variety, competition, cultural relevance, trust, value, and distinctiveness.
Use BRAND_PERSONALITY with the projective prompt 'If [Brand] were a person...' and BRAND_EMOTION with at least Excited, Trusted, Indifferent, and Disappointed.
Use ASPIRATION_GAP to compare the current Fortnite or mobile-gaming experience with the experience respondents ideally want.
Use a price-anchor technique within PAYER_PURCHASE_VALUE or NON_PAYER_SPENDING_BARRIERS without creating price cells or turning the study into a pricing experiment.
Route current, lapsed, competitor-only, payer, and non-payer respondents through the declared branch blocks. Do not create duplicate per-question show-if logic.
Use NPS_SCORE as a 0–10 number rating and place it as the final respondent-facing question and completion point.

Ensure the data supports funnel conversion, competitive repertoire, share of play, usage intensity, brand differentiation, live-service engagement, switching, return, advocacy, monetisation, and segment-comparison analysis.

business_flow.business_goal: Establish a repeatable brand-health tracker to determine how Epic Games and Fortnite are gaining or losing salience, usage, preference, loyalty, advocacy, and competitive share among Indian mobile gamers. The business will use wave-level results to prioritise acquisition, retention, win-back, competitive-conquest, creator, community, live-service, partnership, and monetisation strategies.

dynamic_lists.purpose: Show only brands selected as used in BRAND_TRIAL, preserving the exact option labels and order for comparative quality, value, trust, and innovation ratings.

business_rules.plain_english: Ask BRAND_RECALL_UNAIDED before showing any aided brand list or naming the detailed tracked brands.

If at least one tracked brand or title is selected in BRAND_AWARENESS_AIDED, classify the respondent as brand_aware and continue.
Use BRAND_TRIAL to measure the competitive repertoire and carry only selected trial brands, in the same option order, into COMPETITOR_RATING_GRID.

Use recency anchoring consistently for play, stopping, switching, returning, and purchasing measures across all waves.

Use PAYER_STATUS to route purchasers to purchase behavior and value measures and non-payers to spending barriers and value measures.
Use projective personality, aspiration gap, and a price-anchor approach within the declared questions; the price anchor must not create price cells or experimental assignment.

Apply external quality controls for attention, speed, straight-lining, open-end quality, duplicate records, and implausible behavior. Failed quality cases are quality terminates and must not be classified as non-aware screen-outs.
After NPS_SCORE, complete every respondent who has reached the final loyalty path. No mandatory questions or modules may follow NPS_SCORE.
